squeal: 10s squeal proof scripts/release-identity.test.mjs --base 7b36cf10 --case test --env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2 --env GITHUB_ACTIONS=true 2>&1 | tail -40
firstFinal:
The proof confirms it. I ran `squeal proof` with the old test file at `7b36cf10`, the commit before the fix, against the current code. I set `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2` and `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` on both sides, which is roughly what a CI re-run provides.

| Side | Result |
|---|---|
| Old test (`7b36cf10`) with `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2` | **Fails** |
| Fixed test (HEAD) with the same environment | **Passes** |
| Old test with no such variables | Passes |

The last row is why CI only broke on re-runs: the test was fine whenever the variable was unset.

**Failure in the old test.** The nightly channel expected `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9` and got `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9.2`. The PR channel expected `1.2.3-pr7.9` and got `1.2.3-pr7.9.2`. The release script appends the run attempt to the version when it is greater than 1. The old test's `run()` helper in `scripts/release-identity.test.mjs` leaked the real `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` into the child process.

**Why the old test leaked it.** Its env filter was `GITHUB_ACTIONS$`, which strips only that one `GITHUB_` variable. `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` passed through from the workflow.

**What the fix changes** (`41f16d67`):
- The filter is now `GITHUB_`, so every inherited `GITHUB_*` variable is stripped.
- The test sets `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: '1'` itself, so the expected versions no longer depend on the host.

`7b36cf10`, the commit before the fix, had narrowed the filter from `GITHUB_` to `GITHUB_ACTIONS$` and dropped the pin. That narrowing is what let the variable through.
